chapter_title: Chương 306: Mọi người đều đang cố gắng

segments.title: Chương 306: Mọi người đều đang cố gắng
segments.content:
The Americans' review wasn't over yet, but as it entered its later stages, ByteDance's management was already rehearsing for the roadshow.

The core speakers were Chen Guiliang, who was personally serving as CEO, and Chang Zhongxiang, the CFO. The other senior executives also had to participate. The head of the IPO, Lü Zhihui, would attend in an advisory capacity.

Right now, they were in the internal, private rehearsal phase. Every other day after work, everyone would gather in the conference room to work overtime on it.

The presentation content was determined jointly by the management, investment bank, lawyers, and IR consultants. Everyone had to go through the rehearsals to familiarize themselves with the data, logic, and time allocation within it.

Once the rehearsals reached a certain level, the project team from Goldman Sachs would fly over to simulate investors and ask some sharp questions.

For now, it was Professor Wu and his team of graduate students who came over each evening to play the role of the investor audience, specializing in asking sharp, biting questions to give them a hard time.

The graduate students were in a constant state of excitement, interested in every single step before the IPO. Had they not been personally involved, they would never have known that so much time was spent on mock presentations before the official roadshow.

During the rehearsal process, they were constantly finding faults and making revisions. The PPT deck alone had to be revised countless times.

"Let's go, we're feasting at Jiutouying tonight!" After another day's rehearsal ended, Chen Guiliang called for a meal to boost morale.

"CEO Chen is generous!"

The happiest of all were the group of graduate students.

Almost every time they came to a rehearsal, they were treated to a meal afterward.

At first, it was at the Ziyuan Hotel, then Fuhua Feiniu, Guolin Homestyle Cooking, and Lao Shu Ren. Today, it was Jiutouying's turn. They rotated through various cuisines, all at restaurants near Peking University.

The group of people descended on the place boisterously, chatting and joking on the way.

Everyone had signed non-disclosure agreements, which prohibited discussing the IPO in non-private settings. Even in private settings, they were forbidden from discussing the matter with outsiders. Doing so would be a violation.

Only someone like CEO Liu of Lenovo would not only violate the rules but also proactively brag to reporters about his violation afterward, boasting about how his illicit actions had allowed someone to make money by buying and selling stocks in advance.

Un-lenovo-ble.

"This way, please!" The waiter greeted them enthusiastically.

Jiutouying was a famous chain of Hubei-Hunan cuisine restaurants in the capital, and business had been booming recently.

Because just half a month ago, the owner's wife and son had been kidnapped. It happened right outside the gate of the University of International Business and Economics, where the kidnappers, disguised as traffic police, pulled their car over for an inspection and abducted them in broad daylight.

On the way, they threw his wife out of the car, ordering her to prepare a 10 million RMB ransom for their son.

Four days later, the police caught the culprits and successfully rescued the kidnapped child.

This news became known to everyone in the capital, and in its wake, the main Jiutouying restaurant and its various branches were suddenly flooded with a large number of diners coming to spend money. It didn't have much to do with sympathy; they were mostly just curious and came by to have a meal.

Chen Guiliang led the group into a large private room. They filled two whole tables, and the dishes had already been ordered in advance.

The restaurant specialized in Hubei and Hunan cuisine.

After some idle chat and once two or three dishes had been served, Chen Guiliang raised his glass and said, "Thank you all for your hard work these past days. I'll toast you all!"

Everyone raised their glasses and responded with laughter.

Once the waiter who served the food left the room, they started discussing the day's rehearsal.

The graduate students spoke up enthusiastically, offering their own ideas, suggesting how certain details could be changed to be more reasonable. But then, an American on the team would say that such an idea was wishful thinking and that American investors wouldn't buy it.

The conversation grew more and more lively, and for the most part, it was conducted in English, mainly because they were too lazy to translate for the Americans every time.

Both Chen Guiliang and Xie Yang felt quite a bit of pressure listening to it.

It wasn't just Chen Guiliang who was practicing English; Xie Yang was as well.

In Xie Saobang's own words: "If I'd worked this hard in high school, I would've scored at least a 130 on my English exam and gotten into a top-tier university long ago."

"Knock, knock, knock!"

The waiter was at the door again to serve more dishes.

The group immediately changed the subject. Even though the waiter might not understand English, they still wouldn't talk about this in front of an outsider.

Two more dishes were brought in.

As the waiter was leaving, one of the graduate students asked, "Was it your boss who got kidnapped?"

The waiter had probably been asked this many times and answered patiently, "It wasn't the boss who was kidnapped. It was the boss's wife and son, and they've already been rescued."

"Was it just like in the movies, where they prepared the ransom while also calling the police to catch the bad guys?" someone else asked curiously.

The waiter said, "I'm not too clear on that."

Although the incident had caused a huge stir, the details reported by various media outlets were inconsistent. Even the location where the kidnappers committed the crime was reported differently.

After the waiter left, everyone started chatting again.

Professor Wu remarked with emotion, "I used to only know the general process of an IPO. Now that I'm actually participating, I realize there are so many details. Every single detail is crucial, and a slight mistake anywhere can cause delays."

Ao Yanchen said, "Yeah, it's exhausting enough. We have it easy; CEO Chen already has dark circles under his eyes."

Another Chinese lawyer added, "The truly exhausting part hasn't even started. Half a month of high-intensity roadshows can make a person lose a ton of weight. Flying around all day, dealing with investors' tricky questions, everyone's on edge. Especially CEO Chen. He might suffer from insomnia at night and be so tired during the day he could fall asleep standing up."

Being both insomniac and sleepy, that state was sheer torture.

One of the Americans said, "Of all the Chinese companies going public in the US, ByteDance's progress is relatively fast."

Chen Guiliang took out a pack of Zhonghua cigarettes, lit one for himself, and passed the rest around until the pack was empty.

He took a drag from his cigarette to calm his nerves. He was already exhausted.

The number of cigarettes he smoked, which he had been trying to control, had also noticeably increased during this period. He had no choice but to rely on tobacco to alleviate his anxiety.

Sometimes, he would also comfort himself with the thought that he wasn't the only one who was tired.

Kingsoft, Giant Interactive, Perfect World... they were all currently preparing to go public, and those guys weren't having an easy time either.

Especially Chi Yufeng of Perfect World. He was already on the official roadshow and was expected to list this summer.

A couple of days ago, Chen Guiliang had called Chi Yufeng, and the guy had been mumbling in English. It took him a moment to realize what he was doing before he switched back to Chinese to chat with Chen Guiliang.

With a hint of mischief, Chen Guiliang asked when Perfect World was planning to go public. Chi Yufeng couldn't disclose any information and only said that he had such plans.

After they had eaten and drunk their fill, two drivers drove the large Jinbei vans to take everyone back to their respective residences.

Yang Shuo also drove his sedan, escorting Chen Guiliang all the way back to his house. Because of the Jiutouying kidnapping case, he didn't dare to relax for a moment now, afraid that some kidnappers might target Chen Guiliang.

It was too damn scary, carrying out a kidnapping right outside a university gate!

Chen Guiliang was slightly tipsy at the moment, lying on the living room sofa, not wanting to move. Feeling empty and bored, he called Bian Guanyue to chat.

Bian Guanyue was very hardworking and ambitious. She was studying the material needed for the graduate school entrance exams.

She had also recently signed up for an exam prep class, striving to pass on her first try next year.

After finishing his chat with Bian Guanyue, he called Tao Xue.

Tao Xue was clattering away on her keyboard.
